Root/system identity is available and normal mirroring works, but this HyperOS/Android 16 DisplayManager rejected the secure virtual display (packageName must match the owner uid / SECURE_VD_OEM_REJECT). Magisk elevate alone cannot unlock FLAG_SECURE black screens. Preferred: Magisk enable Zygisk → install ih8SecureLock-scrcpy v10.2 (https://github.com/Ghostpanter/ih8SecureLock-scrcpy/releases/download/v10.2-scrcpy/ih8SecureLock-scrcpy-v10.2-scrcpy.zip) → reboot → do not DenyList target apps → optional disable LSPosed Enable Screenshot → then scrcpy. Secondary: LSPosed + Enable Screenshot (System Framework only, not SystemUI; avoid v5.0.1, prefer v4.2.0). Not bundled. Blind PIN unlock remains available.

On Android 12+, FLAG_SECURE makes the lock screen, encrypted album/gallery previews, and banking/secure apps appear black in the mirror (platform limit; no full view without root). Use this keypad to enter PIN/password blindly. Pattern locks: unlock on the phone first. Encrypted album content cannot be previewed remotely.

Non-root: use Unlock on the mirror for blind PIN/password; unlock patterns on the phone first. On Android 12+ lock screen, encrypted gallery, and FLAG_SECURE apps stay black — encrypted albums cannot be previewed remotely.

Root elevate (optional): off by default — enable 「Elevate server for secure layers」 manually. When on, Magisk su starts the patched server (uid 0, or try uid 1000) and creates a VIRTUAL_DISPLAY_FLAG_SECURE mirror as AID_SYSTEM. Failure falls back to normal mirroring. On HyperOS/A16 Magisk elevate alone often still hits SECURE_VD_OEM_REJECT — prefer the ih8SecureLock-scrcpy Zygisk module above; LSPosed is secondary (below).

Shizuku (local shell): authorize Shizuku on this controller for local shell helpers. Shizuku is only shell uid — it does not replace Root on the target. Android 12+ FLAG_SECURE lock/gallery on the target still need Root elevate there. Wireless ADB always remains available.

Magisk Zygisk module (preferred; verified on MI 9 HyperOS A16): enable Zygisk → install ih8SecureLock-scrcpy v10.2 (download: https://github.com/Ghostpanter/ih8SecureLock-scrcpy/releases/download/v10.2-scrcpy/ih8SecureLock-scrcpy-v10.2-scrcpy.zip) → reboot → do not DenyList target apps → optional: disable LSPosed Enable Screenshot if installed → verify with scrcpy. Repo: https://github.com/Ghostpanter/ih8SecureLock-scrcpy. No LSPosed required; prefer this over the LSPosed steps below. Not bundled in this APK.

LSPosed (secondary; only if not using the Zygisk module above): Magisk Zygisk → JingMatrix LSPosed → Enable Screenshot (Disable FLAG_SECURE; prefer v4.2.0, link in OEM-reject tip) → scope System Framework only → do NOT enable SystemUI → reboot → then scrcpy. Why: scrcpy captures via DisplayManager/SurfaceFlinger in system_server; FLAG_SECURE / encrypted-album blackout is enforced on that framework compose path. Hooking System Framework unlocks the mirror; SystemUI scope only affects SystemUI’s own screenshot/windows and is unnecessary (can hurt). Note: v5.0.1 may break wireless ADB on some HyperOS builds; prefer v4.2.0. This APK does not embed an Xposed module.

Off by default (opt-in; does not auto-force Magisk secure path). When enabled, requests su on connect; tries a secure virtual display as root or AID_SYSTEM. On HyperOS/Android 16, if logs show SECURE_VD_OEM_REJECT, prefer ih8SecureLock-scrcpy Zygisk module above, or the secondary LSPosed steps (not bundled). Normal mirroring still works.

On by default. Install and start Shizuku, then tap the button below to grant. Important: Shizuku provides shell-only access on the controller; on Android 12+, it cannot show the target lock screen or encrypted gallery content (FLAG_SECURE). Those cases require Root elevation on the target.
